entradas.text: “Good afternoon, Mr. President.”
I arrived at the Ministry of Economy and proceeded upstairs. An assistant waiting by the door to the meeting room took my jacket.
“Good afternoon.”
entradas.menu: “Good afternoon.”

entradas.text: I opened the door and entered the largest boardroom in the building. Symon was sitting alone with a glass of water and his documents laid out before him.
A knock was heard on the door and Albin entered the room.
A knock was heard on the door and Gloria entered the room.
A knock was heard on the door and Lucian entered the room.
A knock was heard on the door and Petr entered the room.
“I hope I'm not late.”
“My most sincere apologies. I was attending to other matters.”
“Apologies, I got held up.”
“Sorry, I got held up.”
“Did you start yet?”
“Did you start yet?”
“Did you start yet?”
“Did you start yet?”
“Mr. Vice President. No, not yet.”
“Mrs. Vice President. No, not yet.”
“Now that everyone is here... let's begin.”
“How is it going?”
entradas.menu: “How is it going?”

entradas.text: “Good to see you.”
entradas.menu: “Good to see you.”

entradas.text: “I'm pretty swamped with work. Barely getting any time with the family.”
“Likewise.”
“As you all know, we're here to review the economic progress we've made over the past term and decide how to proceed."
“I will brief you quickly on what we have done so far. Just as a refresher.”
“Very well. Let's hear it."
entradas.menu: “Very well. Let's hear it."

entradas.text: I gestured for Symon to start.
entradas.menu: Gesture for him to begin.

entradas.text: He gathered the documents in the pile in front of him and adjusted his glasses.
“Let's start off with our economy plan.”
“I would like to say we are on track, but unfortunately, I cannot. Our decisions so far have not been in line with our initial intention for a planned economy."
“I am glad to say that we are on track with our intention for a planned economy."
“The economy has taken a hit due to the inconsistence."
“I would like to say we are on track, but unfortunately, I cannot. Our decisions so far have not been in line with our initial intention for a market economy."
“I am glad to say that we are on track with our initial plan for a market economy.”
“We have been largely inconsistent and our economy has taken a hit because of it.”
“Most of our decisions so far have been pretty consistent.”
“Most of our decisions so far have been pretty consistent.”
From the pile, he produced two booklets and handed them to us.
“Please turn to page 5.”
I turned to page 5.
entradas.menu: Turn to page 5.

entradas.text: “I would like to say we are on track, but unfortunately, I cannot. Our decisions so far have not been in line with our initial intention for a market economy."
“It looks like we are going for a mixed approach instead, something in between a market and a planned economy. We have deviated from our plan.”
“I would like to say we are on track, but unfortunately, I cannot. Our decisions so far have not been in line with our initial intention for a planned economy."
“It looks like we are going for a mixed approach instead, something between a planned and a market economy.”
“If I were to describe what we have done so far, I would say that it is very close to a laissez-faire economic system.”
“If I were to describe what we have done so far, I would say that it is very close to a full command economic system.”
“Which leaves us horribly equipped for the war we're about to enter."
“War is always costly, and our economy will suffer tremendously no matter what. The real question here is how much.”
“Which leaves us exceptionally well-equipped for the war we are about to enter.”
“That said, war is always costly and our economy will suffer no matter what. The real question here is how much.”
“Whatever the state of the economy right now, I have to inform you that the war we're about to enter will make it worse.”
“And my answer to that is, it is hard to say at this point. It depends on how long it will go on for and whether we are on the winning side.”
“And my answer to that is, it is hard to say at this point. It depends on how long it will go on for and whether we are on the winning side.”
“Please turn to page 16.”
I turned to page 16, titled "Status of Trade and the Effects of Foreign Policy".

entradas.text: “Please turn to page 16.”
I turned to page 16, titled "Status of Trade and the Effects of Foreign Policy".

entradas.text: “I am happy to say that our trade has increased since the beginning of our term.”
“We are on the right path. More trade means a more vibrant economy, which means unbridled economic development.”
“Our economy has the potential to stagnate unless we open up further and chase after more trade deals.”
“I am sad to say that our trade has decreased since the beginning of our term.”
“For better or for worse, Sordland is becoming quite reliant on foreign economies.”
“Having said that, the fact that we're now able to rely completely on our own economy is definitely a step in the right direction.”
I turned to page 17.
entradas.menu: Turn to page 17.

entradas.text: “Please turn to page 17.”
“In our attempt to repair Sordland's economic system, we have generally sided with businesses.”
“In our attempt to repair Sordland's economic system, we have mostly gone against the wishes of big business in favour of the requests of Sordish citizens.”
“In our attempt to repair Sordland's economic system, we went for a mixed approach. We tried to cater to the needs of both businesses and Sordish citizens."
“Even though the country benefited financially, the people certainly weren't fond of it.”
“This caused us to take on some losses in order to make the people happy.”
“It's been a delicate balance."
“Thankfully, living standards are steadily increasing. We've been receiving fewer and fewer complaints about our welfare systems.”
“The bad news is, our living standards are decreasing. We've been receiving more and more complaints about our welfare systems.”
“Meanwhile, businesses are enjoying a lower tax rate compared to the start of our term.”
“Meanwhile, businesses are certainly not pleased with the higher taxes we've imposed on them."
“Now, to page 34.”
I turned to page 34.

entradas.text: “Production in our country has nearly doubled since the start of our administration. It is a great success.”
“Our production rate has gone down since the beginning of the term. We're at a low point right now."
“We have an infrastructure problem, and the economy won't truly flourish unless we solve it.”
“Our situation has improved above and beyond our expectations."
“We are very close to the end. I want to talk about a few numbers. Please turn to page 57. I have prepared a chart.”
I turned to page 57.
entradas.menu: Turn to page 57.

entradas.text: “Our inflation rate is currently at an amazing 2%, down from 10%. It's the lowest Sordland has ever seen.”
“Our inflation rate is currently at a staggering 49%, way up from 10%. It might be the highest in Sordland's history."
“Our inflation rate is currently at 24%, up from 10%, which leaves a lot to be desired.”
“Our current debt is at 611 billion SR, up from 427 billion SR at the beginning of our term.”
“Our debt is at 310 billion SR, down from 427 billion SR at the beginning of our term.”
“Our debt is at 428 billion SR, close to 427 billion SR at the beginning of our term.”
“Our current GDP is at 513 billion SR. A major increase from the 310 billion SR we had at the beginning of our term.”
“Our current GDP is at 141 billion SR. A major decrease from the 310 billion SR we had at the beginning of our term.”
“Our current GDP is at 314 billion SR. Not much more than the 310 billion SR we had at the beginning of our term.”
“The unemployment rate is at 5%, down from 16%.”
“The unemployment rate is at 24%, up from 16%.”
“The unemployment rate remains steady at 16%."
“I want to quickly highlight our budget expenditure.”
“My numbers indicate that overall, we have been generously spending our government budget.”
“My numbers indicate that overall, we have been fairly conservative with our government budget."
“My numbers indicate that overall, we have been fairly balanced in spending our government budget."
“Money that is not spent is just pieces of paper, so that's good for us.”
“It's a good virtue to think ahead, but we ought to remember that money that is not spent is just pieces of paper."
“A balanced approach is good, however, we shouldn't forget that money that is not spent is just pieces of paper.”
“Now, going into the elections and hopefully a second term, we need to decide on the way forward.”
“Now, going into the elections and hopefully a second term, we need to decide on the way forward.”
“One thing is clear. We need a bigger budget."
“What should we do, Mr. President? Any ideas?”
“What should we do, Mr. President? Any ideas?”
“One thing is clear. Our economy is solid enough that we can start thinking big."
“We will take an international loan from MFI.”

entradas.text: “We will print more money.”

entradas.text: “This will create quite a risk in case of an actual emergency, but it can be done.”
“I'll get right on it after this meeting.”
“This will pose quite a risk to our economy, but it can be done.”
“This will pose quite a risk to the reputation of our administration, but it can be done.”
“We will pay back all student debts.”
entradas.menu: “We will pay back all student debts. [-2 Government Budget]”

entradas.text: “We will pay an unemployment wage so the jobless do not go hungry."
entradas.menu: “We will pay an unemployment wage so the jobless do not go hungry." [-2 Government Budget]”

entradas.text: “We will provide housing assistance to all citizens who require it."
entradas.menu: “We will provide housing assistance to all citizens who require it. [-2 Government Budget]”

entradas.text: “I'll get right on it."
“That is an excellent idea.”
“That's all, then.”
“Thank you for coming.”
The meeting dispersed. I hurried to the cafeteria to get a cup of coffee.

“Have some faith. We will win, I assure you.”

“We had to make sacrifices and cuts.”

“As you wish, sir.”

“Of course we had to. But we might have made the wrong ones.”

“It was certainly justifiable if you ask me.”

“Teamwork makes it happen.”
“I understand the excitement. As much as I would like production to increase even further, we will need to take it one step at a time."
“We're on the right track. If we keep doing what we are doing, it is bound to get better.”
"I suggest we tackle the problem before pointing fingers.”
“I'll note that down."
“What matters is the big picture.”
“Our infrastructure projects have paid off in the long term.”
“Smoother commutes, easier access, faster delivery times -- everybody's happy.”

“Good news for the Sordish people.”

“It's not the end of the world. Look at everything else we've been able to accomplish.”

“It's not the end of the world. Look at all the other stuff we've been able to accomplish."
“Our image won't suffer for this if we're able to redirect the public's attention toward our other accomplishments.”
“We are writing history here.”

entradas.text: “Good. We need all the help we can get for the election.”
